A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TESSERA and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v6 reports original classification, segmentation, and regression experiments in Table 1, plus ablations, robustness tests, and additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: v7 retains those original experiments and adds spatial-context ablations and evaluations on Togo and Ethiopian crop datasets in Appendices A.5–A.6.

M1.justification: The dual encoders, temporal sampling, fusion, quantization, Barlow Twins and mixup objectives, global shuffling, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The new spatial variants are experimental ablations, not changes to the proposed TESSERA model.

E1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds CropHarvest Togo and Ethiopian crop classification evaluations. These substantially extend agricultural evaluation beyond Austria and France to Sub-Saharan smallholder populations and different seasonal conditions. Existing datasets and task families are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original experiments is unchanged. New Table 5 reuses existing baselines: CROMA for Togo and AlphaEarth for Ethiopia. The spatial-input variants are TESSERA ablations rather than new external comparison methods.

E3.justification: New Figure 12 introduces a comparison under a 100-PFLOPS budget using 1×1, 3×3, and 15×15 inputs, with 30% Austrian Crop labels and full PASTIS-R/Borneo labels. Existing evaluation settings are retained. Splits and label budgets for the new African evaluations are not specified.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 and Figure 12 add a targeted test of whether spatial patches improve representations across classification, segmentation, and canopy-height regression, alongside a 2017 Borneo artifact visualization. The existing component, seasonal-window, cloud, and scaling analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 12 newly reports 10, 5, and 20 repeats for Austrian Crop, PASTIS-R, and Borneo, respectively, with ± uncertainty entries. The uncertainty statistic is not defined. Existing repetition and error-bar reporting is retained; no increase in runs for existing experiments is established.

E6.justification: Matched existing results are unchanged. New Table 5 reports Togo F1 of 83.01 for TESSERA versus 79.15 for CROMA, and Ethiopian accuracy of 44.92 versus approximately 41 for AlphaEarth. Within new Figure 12, increasing inputs from 1×1 to 15×15 improves PASTIS-R mIoU from 36.92 to 37.33 but worsens Borneo RMSE from 15.45 to 18.25. These are additional experiments, not improvements over v6 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss formulations, metric expressions, and both pseudocode algorithms are unchanged. The added spatial-context and geographic explanations introduce no formal derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of robust, label-efficient temporal embeddings, strong downstream performance, and open global annual 10 m embedding products. The new experiments support the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 adds the argument that fixed spatial priors and clear-patch requirements reduce data availability and cause artifacts. Appendix A.6 interprets African results as evidence that spectral trends support local seasonality despite weak temporal priors. These extend the previous mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v7 removes Section 3.4 details about 96 Intel inference GPUs, approximately 5 PB of annual input, 300 TB of annual embeddings, and release ordering. It also directs the abstract's code/data link to the specific TESSERA repository rather than the organization page. These are documentation and access-instruction changes, not established changes to execution.

R1.justification: v7 adds CropHarvest, Ethiopian crop-data, and GeoTessera software references and corrects the SpectralEarth citation. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning against prior embedding-based models remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v7 inserts two appendix subsections and an acknowledgments section, makes localized wording edits, and removes an unresolved 'Figure ??' reference. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v7 adds Figure 12 and Table 5, with subsequent displays renumbered and reflowed. Figure 4(a) loses an unlabeled dashed horizontal line while its plotted results remain unchanged. The existing visual design and other figure content are retained.

improvement.justification: The controlled spatial ablation strengthens evidence for the central pixel-wise design, and the African evaluations broaden geographic validation. The gain is limited: Appendix A.6 omits detailed protocols and claims superiority to both baselines on both datasets although Table 5 reports only one comparator per dataset. Removed inference-resource details also reduce documentation. The added diagnostic evidence nevertheless provides a modest net improvement.
